exercise.name: Cable Lying Extension Pullover (with rope attachment)
aliases: Lying cable triceps extension to pullover

reference.title: Cable Lying Extension Pullover (with rope attachment)
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (proxy refused gymvisual.com), so the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)

exercise.mechanics: Compound (elbow extension with shoulder flexion and extension)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in as the rope goes back behind the head, breathe out as you pull it over and extend the arms.
breathing.cadence: About 2.4 s back, short stretch, about 1.8 s up

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Cable stack load is user-chosen and moderate: the lower back stays on the bench.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then one plate on the stack

cues.text: Lie face up on a flat bench with the head toward a low pulley, feet flat; rope ends in both hands, arms straight up over the chest, palms facing.
Breathe in; bend the elbows and let the upper arms travel back past the head so the rope goes down behind the head, elbows pointing to the pulley.
Stretch with the elbows bent and the upper arms beside the head; ribs down, lower back on the bench.
Breathe out; pull the elbows up over the face (pullover) while straightening them, finishing with the arms straight over the chest.
Squeeze the triceps with the arms straight, then lower again.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the lower back at the stretch
mistakes.fix: Keep the ribs down; stop the upper arms beside the head.
Keep the elbows about shoulder width.
Use a weight you can control behind the head.

kinematics.norm: From straight to about 85-110 degrees behind the head (clinical opinion)
Upper arms from vertical to about 60 degrees past vertical, beside the head; pullover movements engage the lats and pectoralis (Teixeira 2022, Campos 2014)
Neutral on the rope ends (clinical opinion)
Low pulley behind the head (clinical opinion)
Head, upper back and buttocks on the bench, feet planted (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 2.4 s back and 1.8 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Cable Lying Extension Pullover (with rope attachment), video (movement reference)

The different role of each head of the triceps brachii muscle in elbow extension (Acta Orthop Traumatol Turc 2018;52(3):201-205; PubMed 29503079; EMG plus OpenSim at 0-180 degrees of shoulder elevation)

Teixeira, Gomes, da Silva, Magalhães and Marchetti 2022, differences between pullover and pulldown exercises on maximal isometric force and myoelectric activity in recreationally-trained men (Int J Exerc Sci 15(4):797-807; PMC9362894)
Campos and Silva 2014, comparison of electromyographic activity during the bench press and barbell pullover exercises (Motriz 20(2):200-205)

Triceps brachii hypertrophy is substantially greater after elbow extension training performed in the overhead versus neutral arm position (Eur J Sport Sci 2022, DOI 10.1080/17461391.2022.2100279; PubMed 35819335; 21 adults, 12 weeks, cable)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
The cable load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can move with the trunk still and the shoulders down.
Bring the rope up over the chest before sitting up.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort overhead: keep the upper arms more vertical (lying triceps extension only).
Lower-back discomfort: feet on the end of the bench.

muscleNotes.triceps_r: Prime mover: straightens the elbows; the long head also helps bring the arm down from overhead.
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Prime mover: straightens the elbows; the long head also helps bring the arm down from overhead.
muscleNotes.lats_r: Prime mover of the pullover: brings the upper arms from overhead back over the chest.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Prime mover of the pullover: brings the upper arms from overhead back over the chest.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Helps bring the arm down from overhead.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Helps bring the arm down from overhead.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Holds the shoulder blades on the rib cage.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Holds the shoulder blades on the rib cage.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the ribs down and the back on the bench.
